reference_answer: Deleting a document marks its global ID deleted and removes the external-ID mapping, but does not erase the physical forward row/doc_ids entry. Physical=28 and live=25; stats applies the deletion filter. Upsert behavior is optional for this delete-only task. Vector storage already exists before optimize: non-quantized inserts create default FLAT memory vector indexers; flush transfers them to persisted vector_indexers. A new HNSW-schema segment lacks the requested-index built flag (only an initially FLAT schema is pre-marked). The first nonempty optimize materializes the requested HNSW index. With physical=28/live=25 the strict live < physical * (1 - 0.3f) purge test is false, so the sealed single-segment group gets CreateVectorIndexTask and no coordinated forward-row purge. The in-place index-build helper passes the segment deletion filter into Merge. The filter resolves original row positions to deleted global IDs. Merge enables PK rewrite and the reducer skips filtered vectors while assigning surviving vectors consecutive IDs. Forward rows/doc_ids and new block metadata retain physical positions/counts, so compact vector keys no longer denote the same forward rows. Search keys are interpreted as segment row indices when fetching forward IDs/fields; point vector fetch uses the original physical row/block offset. This explains wrong associations and high-row vector-fetch failure while scalar-only access and live counts can agree. Flushed replacement index/metadata and reload explain why reopening is not a repair. Do not reduce the fault to harmless ANN recall or missing scalar rows. Empty optimize has no persisted content to process. Clean nonempty first materialization has no tombstones, so it preserves key alignment and records the target index as built. The later delete-only same-segment/same-parameter create_vector_index returns early on the indexed flag. This explains the exact controls, not universal directory immunity. Above the deletion threshold, true CompactTask passes the delete filter through scalar reduction, constructs a bitmap of omitted original row positions, and uses the matching row filter for vector reduction. Both spaces are compacted together. Therefore skipping tombstoned vectors is appropriate there, unlike a vector-only rebuild over unchanged forward rows. A vector-only rebuild must retain tombstoned vector slots when forward rows are unchanged; or both sides would need coordinated remapping. Passing no deletion filter on the former path is the targeted correction, while deletion filtering at query time and coordinated full compaction remain necessary. The essential oracle supplies independent known normalized directions, such as unit basis vectors, and checks the expected live ID and vector payload after the below-threshold delete/optimize sequence. It must detect wrong association rather than only counts; an affected-index fetch or same-ID query is not an independent vector oracle. Wider variant coverage is useful but optional for this single point.

success_rule.rule: source_grounded_success = nonempty final answer AND total_points >= 8 AND C2 == 2 AND C3 == 2 AND all core citation gates pass AND no substantiated disqualifying overclaim or critical contradiction. Any such disqualification forces failure independently of points.

critical_contradictions: C1: The single-segment vector-only path compacts forward rows in coordination with the filtered vectors, while identifying that same path as the cause.
C2: There is no vector/forward association error; the scenario is solely ordinary approximate-search recall loss.
C3: Read-only reopening repairs the persisted vector-key mapping.
C4: Disabling tombstone filtering during queries is the repair.
C5: No vector storage or vector indexer exists before the first optimize, or an existing default FLAT indexer means the requested HNSW index is already marked built.
D1: Treat the original tail-only description as complete and explicitly deny wrong-vector associations.
D2: Every overwrite/delete followed by optimize is affected regardless of the maintenance path.
D3: Repairing only absent tail rows with vectors fetched from the affected index fully repairs all wrong associations.
D4: Assert a local runtime reproduction or passing upstream test execution without supporting execution evidence.

Segment counts distinguish physical doc_ids_ entries from live non-deleted entries.

The configured compaction deletion ratio is 0.3f.

VectorColumnIndexer::Merge forwards the row filter into the core index merge.
The core merge configures the reducer to rewrite primary keys.
The reducer skips filtered vectors and assigns consecutive output keys to the surviving vectors.
Scalar document fetch resolves retained physical row positions and checks logical deletion.
Point vector fetch resolves vector blocks using original physical row positions and block offsets.
Combined vector search returns keys in the segment row coordinate space.
Vector recall uses returned row keys to retrieve forward IDs and fields.
Read filtering preserves logical deletion independently of vector-index rebuilding.
Coordinated compaction filters scalar data and applies corresponding filtering while building vectors.
Full scalar compaction rewrites forward rows and their document-ID mapping together.
Full compaction records filtered original positions in a bitmap shared with vector filtering.
Compaction results are committed through persisted metadata and loaded into the collection.
Creation pre-marks requested vector indexes only for an initially FLAT schema, not the HNSW schema in this task.
Segment metadata tracks whether a requested vector field index has been built.
Non-quantized insertion initializes a memory vector indexer with default index parameters.
The default non-quantized vector index parameters select FLAT storage.
Flush transfers memory vector indexers into persisted vector blocks with physical counts.
Successful requested-index building records the indexed vector field in segment metadata.
A later same-parameter create_vector_index returns early when the requested index is already marked built.
Scalar forward scans apply the segment deletion predicate to physical row IDs.
The scalar predicate maps local rows to global IDs and tests the deletion filter.
